note: Keys whose sentence changes with a count. English needs two forms and other languages need more, so the catalogue carries plural variations rather than one form with an appended (s). The variation argument is the 1-based position of the counted specifier in the format string.

fleet.none.match.one: %lld Spark is paired with this device. None of them match the current search and filters.
fleet.none.match.other: %lld Sparks are paired with this device. None of them match the current search and filters.

preflight.netplan.one: %lld network configuration file already on this Spark
preflight.netplan.other: %lld network configuration files already on this Spark

dashboard.recipes.snapshot.one: %lld verified recipe in the device-local snapshot
dashboard.recipes.snapshot.other: %lld verified recipes in the device-local snapshot

merge.contested.regions.one: %lld region was rewritten on both devices and stays marked.
merge.contested.regions.other: %lld regions were rewritten on both devices and stay marked.

chat.shares.unreadable.count.one: %lld shared item could not be read. Removing it keeps every readable share.
chat.shares.unreadable.count.other: %lld shared items could not be read. Removing them keeps every readable share.

inference.verdict.answering.rate.one: Answering %lld request at %@ tokens per second.
inference.verdict.answering.rate.other: Answering %lld requests at %@ tokens per second.

intent.error.too.large.one: This action accepts up to %lld byte. Open SparkPilot for larger work.
intent.error.too.large.other: This action accepts up to %lld bytes. Open SparkPilot for larger work.

pairing.join.code.locked.one: Too many join codes were tried on this Spark, so it is not accepting any for about %lld minute. Your code stays valid until it expires; try again after the wait.
pairing.join.code.locked.other: Too many join codes were tried on this Spark, so it is not accepting any for about %lld minutes. Your code stays valid until it expires; try again after the wait.

substitution_note: A sentence whose count sits beside other arguments needs a named substitution rather than a whole-string plural: the variation applies to one clause and the rest of the sentence stays put. `template` is the English sentence with positional specifiers and the substitution token; the generator checks that its non-substitution specifiers are the ones the compiler emitted for the same key.

status.load.model.waiting.name: jobs
status.load.model.waiting.template: %1$@ is loaded, unified memory is %2$lld percent used, and %#@jobs@.

status.load.none.waiting.name: jobs
status.load.none.waiting.template: No model is loaded, unified memory is %1$lld percent used, and %#@jobs@.

preflight.conflict.port.name: ports
preflight.conflict.port.template: Something on this Spark is already using %#@ports@ %2$@, which Spark Runtime needs.

preflight.conflict.port.recovery.name: ports
preflight.conflict.port.recovery.template: Stop or move whatever is listening on %#@ports@ %2$@, then check this Spark again. Spark Runtime will not take a port from a service you are already running.

preflight.conflict.unit.name: units
preflight.conflict.unit.template: This Spark already has %#@units@ %2$@, but no Spark Runtime package that would explain it.

preflight.conflict.unit.recovery.name: units
preflight.conflict.unit.recovery.template: Remove %#@units@ %2$@, then check this Spark again. Installing would replace a service this app did not put there.

telemetry.history.minute.name: readings
telemetry.history.minute.template: An average of %#@readings@ over one minute.

onboarding.rediscovery.elapsed.name: minutes
onboarding.rediscovery.elapsed.template: %1$@ elapsed. Sparks usually come back within a few minutes; the search stops after %#@minutes@.

onboarding.restart.hold.name: seconds
onboarding.restart.hold.template: Watching for the Spark to begin restarting. Checks start anyway in %#@seconds@.

onboarding.restart.elapsed.name: minutes
onboarding.restart.elapsed.template: %1$@ elapsed. Checking every few seconds; the wait stops after %#@minutes@.

catalogue.published.available.name: recipes
catalogue.published.available.template: New: %#@recipes@ published, different from this Spark's snapshot

uncounted_note: Keys the counted-copy gate would flag whose word after the count is not the noun being counted. Each entry says why, and the gate rejects an entry that no longer matches a declared key.

uncounted.chat.attachment.pdf.blank.page: the word after the page number is the verb 'has', not a noun agreeing with it
